Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed mass with sharp margins and homogeneous opacity in the right hemithorax, which is a classic radiographic presentation for Pleuropulmonary Synovial Sarcoma (PPSS). This appearance distinguishes it from primary lung carcinomas that typically exhibit ill-defined or spiculated borders.
